safety_verdicts.content: Her normal bowel habit is once per day.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not document baseline bowel habit of once daily.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Baseline bowel habit (once daily) helps contextualize the acuity of symptoms but is unlikely to change immediate management of an apparent acute gastroenteritis episode. Omission mainly reduces documentation completeness rather than altering safety-critical decisions.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient’s mother also had similar symptoms and patient was in contact with her.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention mother having similar symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Missing additional household contact symptoms/exposure could slightly affect assessment of infectious spread and counseling on infection control, but typically would not change urgent dehydration-focused management. The impact is primarily on epidemiologic context and follow-up advice.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not explicitly document absence of rash.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting absence of rash has minimal effect in a GI-predominant presentation and is unlikely to change triage or treatment. This is largely a completeness issue unless rash would have suggested an alternative systemic diagnosis.

safety_verdicts.content: Mother also experienced similar gastrointestinal symptoms.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention mother having similar GI symptoms.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that another family member had similar GI symptoms can reduce confidence in a contagious etiology and misses an opportunity for targeted public-health/infection-control advice, but does not typically alter the immediate care plan. Clinical harm is limited to reduced situational awareness and counseling.

safety_verdicts.content: No previous abdominal problems or surgery
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Transcript supports no previous abdominal problems, but does not explicitly confirm no prior surgery; the combined statement overreaches.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting “no prior surgery” when it was not confirmed could mislead future clinicians; prior abdominal surgery can meaningfully change differential diagnosis and risk assessment for abdominal pain (e.g., adhesions/obstruction). In this case it is not immediately injurious but could cause downstream diagnostic error if relied upon.
